questions.question: When you start an engine, what should happen?

options.text: Warning lights turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn on for a few seconds, then turn off. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal when you start a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal within a few seconds after starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or unstable.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always dangerous because the driver cannot see everything behind them. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: When driving a tank vehicle with liquid cargo, you should:

options.text: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when driving with liquid cargo. This reduces sudden braking, which can cause the liquid to surge inside the tank.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Required only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how short.

questions.question: In poor weather, many drivers:

options.text: Like to drive in front of trucks.

questions.explanation: In bad weather, many drivers follow large trucks too closely, especially when visibility is poor.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Not light up or sound at all.
Turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn on, then quickly turn off.

questions.question: The best way to notice a trailer skid is by:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors to see if your trailer is skidding or jackknifing. This helps you spot the problem as early as possible.

questions.question: If you skid from going too fast, you can usually fix it by:

options.text: Taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Simply remove your foot from the accelerator to fix a skid caused by going too fast. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: Look into the back of the fifth wheel:

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: During a coupling inspection, look under the trailer into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: An exhaust system should be:
questions.explanation: All exhaust system parts must be firmly attached. Check that nothing is loose, broken, or missing. Parts should not rub against any moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher, unless it is transporting hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher, unless it will travel through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down firmly for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the pedal does not return to normal position, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down firmly for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the brake pedal three times, then push down firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other brake system problem.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent a truck from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping the cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent rollover, load cargo as low as possible and drive slowly around turns. Driving on road shoulders does not help prevent rollover.

questions.question: If a driver is given a leaking package, they should:

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse any leaking packages or shipments of hazardous materials.

questions.question: Surge is strongest in:
questions.explanation: Tanks without internal bulkheads allow liquid to flow freely. These tanks are most at risk for surge.

questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light stays on after starting the engine, it means:

options.text: The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light should turn on when you start the engine, then turn off. If the light stays on, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tires with only 3/32 of an inch of tread

questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread. All tires on a vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.3 materials, the floor liner should be:
questions.explanation: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials, use a floor liner made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal. The floor must be tight. Non-ferrous metals contain no iron.

questions.question: When driving a tank vehicle, surge:
questions.explanation: Liquid surge in a tank can cause serious handling problems. For example, a forward surge could push a stopped vehicle into an intersection.
